title: Freedom and Responsibility
text:
Existentialist thinkers argue that human beings are not born with a fixed essence, but create their identity through the choices they make. Sartre famously claimed that existence precedes essence, meaning that a person first exists and only afterwards defines what they are. This absence of predetermined meaning can feel liberating, yet it also produces a profound sense of anxiety.

For this reason, existentialists insist that freedom carries an inescapable burden of responsibility. Since no external authority can justify our decisions, each person must own the consequences of their actions. Camus, by contrast, emphasised that the search for meaning in an indifferent universe can itself be a source of dignity.

questions.text: According to Sartre's claim in the first paragraph, what comes first?
What do existentialists say freedom carries?
options: A fixed set of moral rules

questions.text: Why must each person own the consequences of their actions?
options: Because external authority can justify all decisions
Because no external authority can justify our decisions
Because society assigns blame at random

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about Camus's view of meaning?
options: It can be found only through religious faith
It is absent, so the search for it is pointless
The search itself can give dignity even in an indifferent universe
It is determined by one's essence

paragraph_translations: Los pensadores existencialistas sostienen que los seres humanos no nacen con una esencia fija, sino que crean su identidad mediante las decisiones que toman. Sartre afirmó de manera célebre que la existencia precede a la esencia, lo que significa que una persona primero existe y solo después define lo que es. Esta ausencia de un sentido predeterminado puede resultar liberadora, pero también produce una profunda sensación de ansiedad.

Por esta razón, los existencialistas insisten en que la libertad conlleva una carga ineludible de responsabilidad. Como ninguna autoridad externa puede justificar nuestras decisiones, cada persona debe asumir las consecuencias de sus actos. Camus, en cambio, subrayó que la búsqueda de sentido en un universo indiferente puede ser en sí misma una fuente de dignidad.
